key_insight: A two-stage quantum-classical pipeline uses LR-QAOA with cycle-edge encoding to generate feasible distribution-network topologies, then steers a MISOCP solver toward lower-loss reconfiguration solutions.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a hardware-aware way to accelerate distribution network reconfiguration while respecting spanning-tree feasibility and electrical constraints.
method: Cycle-edge encoding restricts the quantum search space to spanning-tree configurations.
Iterative LR-QAOA samples feasible topologies within a qubit-budgeted subspace.
Hardware-derived samples guide a downstream MISOCP solver to refine the best topology.
evidence_signal: Across six benchmark networks (33 to 417 buses), hardware-guided MISOCP reached an incumbent within 1% of the best-known solution in less median solver time than an unguided solver.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the sampled quantum distribution transfers to the classical optimizer, and the approach may be limited by qubit budget and hardware noise.
paper_title: Two-Stage Quantum-Classical Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Cycle-Edge Encoding
